title: From Copilots to Agents: Rebuilding the Company Around AI

reader_summary.headline: When you're building AI, the first thing that you need to build is the breaks of the system.
reader_summary.overview: When you're building AI, the first thing that you need to build is the breaks of the system. It's the understanding on where you're going to deploy it and how you're going to deploy it. We had thousands and millions of information lines about our users.

key_points.text: And the first thing that we did was we just built the system that allowed us to understand everything about every user.
key_points.evidence_quote: And the first thing that we did was we just built the system that allowed us to understand everything about every user.

key_points.text: We built these co-pilot tools and we realized very quickly they didn't adopt them.
key_points.evidence_quote: We built these co-pilot tools and we realized very quickly they didn't adopt them.

key_points.text: So we went funnel by funnel, putting agents in front of like critical aspects of the business.
key_points.evidence_quote: So we went funnel by funnel, putting agents in front of like critical aspects of the business.

key_points.text: We put the agents in front of our users really quickly.
key_points.evidence_quote: We put the agents in front of our users really quickly.

thesis: The discussion argues that building AI requires first establishing the system's breaks to understand deployment, noting that while co-pilot tools often fail adoption, agents can successfully handle critical business aspects. It further illustrates this by detailing how Kavak replaced non-adopted co-pilot tools with agents that now manage over 90% of customer interactions, a transition that required a year of flat growth but was driven by the founder's background in adapting to change and recognizing human patterns.
